title: Bug: Parallel RFS builds race on shared ./fsroot directory when multiple DEPENDENT_MACHINEs exist
author: aajith-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

broadcom

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

When an installer target has multiple `DEPENDENT_MACHINE` entries (e.g.`broadcom-dnx` and `broadcom-legacy`), the RFS squashfs targets for the dependent machines run in parallel but all use the same hardcoded `FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot` in `build_debian.sh`.
One build's `rm -rf ./fsroot` clobbers the other's in-progress debootstrap extraction, causing a tar failure.

This was introduced in #25192 (March 2026), which added `broadcom-legacy` as a second `DEPENDENT_MACHINE`. Previously only `broadcom-dnx` was a dependent, and since the main `broadcom` RFS target depends on it via `DEPENDENT_RFS`, they ran sequentially. With two independent dependents, make runs them in parallel, causing the problem.

### Steps to Reproduce


  1. `make configure PLATFORM=broadcom`
  2. `make target/sonic-broadcom.bin SONIC_BUILD_JOBS=16`



### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual:**
Both `sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-dnx__rfs.squashfs` and `sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-legacy__rfs.squashfs` launch concurrently and call `build_debian.sh`, which does:

```
  FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot        # build_debian.sh:42, hardcoded
  # ...
  sudo rm -rf $FILESYSTEM_ROOT    # line 86
  mkdir -p $FILESYSTEM_ROOT       # line 88
  # debootstrap into $FILESYSTEM_ROOT ...
```
Both RFS builds clobber each other's `./fsroot`. debootstrap fails during package extraction.

**Expected:**
 Each RFS target should use its own filesystem root directory so parallel builds don't interfere

**Suggested fix:**
Note that `onie-image.conf` already has `${FILESYSTEM_ROOT:=./fsroot-${TARGET_MACHINE}}` as a default, and the ARM configs (`onie-image-armhf.conf`, `onie-image-arm64.conf`) already use `./fsroot-${TARGET_MACHINE}`. The hardcoded assignment in `build_debian.sh` overrides
   this before `onie-image.conf` is sourced.

The hardcoded assignment can be removed.

### Relevant log output

```shell
[ 01 ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-dnx__rfs.squashfs ]
  [ 02 ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-legacy__rfs.squashfs ]

  [ FAIL LOG START ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-legacy__rfs.squashfs ]
  Build start time: Sun Apr 12 19:52:19 UTC 2026
  + FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot
  + scripts/build_debian_base_system.sh amd64 trixie ./fsroot
  I: Valid Release signature (key id 41587F7DB8C774BCCF131416762F67A0B2C39DE4)
  I: Chosen extractor for .deb packages: dpkg-deb
  I: Extracting bsdutils...
  E: Tried to extract package, but tar failed. Exit...
  [  FAIL LOG END  ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-legacy__rfs.squashfs ]
  make: *** [slave.mk:1411: target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-legacy__rfs.squashfs] Error 1

  [ FAIL LOG START ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-dnx__rfs.squashfs ]
  Build start time: Sun Apr 12 19:52:18 UTC 2026
  + FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot
  I: Extracting bsdutils...
  E: Tried to extract package, but tar failed. Exit...
  [  FAIL LOG END  ] [ target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-dnx__rfs.squashfs ]
  make: *** [slave.mk:1411: target/sonic-broadcom.bin__broadcom-dnx__rfs.squashfs] Error 1
```

```shell

```

comments.author: Bojun-Feng
comments.body:
Hmm, I believe currently in `build_debian.sh` we are running `onie-image.conf` after defining `FILESYSTEM_ROOT`, and before removing / creating the directory:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/a11c997b50c257569e96b76aa8bf220bb4eb3fd4/build_debian.sh#L38-L48

However, `onie-image.conf` defines the filesystem root properly and overwrites the definition for `FILESYSTEM_ROOT`.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/a11c997b50c257569e96b76aa8bf220bb4eb3fd4/onie-image.conf#L16

@aajith-arista would you mind sharing the commit or branch you are building from? If it is from the current master, the root cause may be something different.

That said, the current hardcoded `FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot` in `build_debian.sh` is dead code and should probably be removed. Happy to file a PR for this.

linkedPullRequests.title: [build] Fix parallel RFS build race condition on shared fsroot
linkedPullRequests.author: rustiqly
linkedPullRequests.body: Fixes #26733. Removed dead code in build_debian.sh that hardcoded FILESYSTEM_ROOT=./fsroot, which caused parallel dependent RFS builds to clobber each other's directories.

Rechecked CI for https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26759.

The current required completed failure is `Azure.sonic-buildimage (Test Trivy vulnerability scan (docker-ptf))` from Azure build `1110942` / GitHub run https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/runs/75418916380. This looks unrelated to the RFS `fsroot` race fix in this PR:

- `docker-ptf` Trivy scan reports pre-existing Debian 12.13 package CVEs and Go stdlib CVEs
- Trivy also reports private-key files inside the `docker-ptf` image contents
- this PR only removes the shared `./fsroot` path from the RFS build command and does not change `docker-ptf`
- the visible `Build broadcom` / `Build aspeed_arm64` failures are canceled checks from superseded Azure build `1110888`; several jobs from rerun `1110942` passed and some Elastictest jobs are still pending

Requesting a fresh Azure run so the required checks are not blocked by this unrelated scan/canceled-run state.

CI update for https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26759: the latest required Azure failure is still isolated to `Azure.sonic-buildimage (Test Trivy vulnerability scan (docker-ptf))` in build `1111046`.

I checked the log: `docker-ptf` is a cached/base image scan failure, not a failure caused by this RFS race-condition change. The scan reports Debian/Go package CVEs in existing image contents (`liblcms2-2`, `wireshark*`, `linux-libc-dev`, Go `stdlib`) and the known generated/default private-key findings under `/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key` and `/etc/ssl/private/ssl-cert-snakeoil.key`.

All other required Azure build and Elastictest checks are green in the current report.
